RagShortTexts: The standing military of Vandals in 374 AD relied upon veteran formations specialized in disciplined field deployment.
Combining heavy protective armor with specialized assault weaponry, the troops executed tactical doctrines honed in frontier engagements.
Commanders emphasized coordinated shock charges and defensive stability, preventing frontline collapse against aggressive cavalry raids.

Variants.Content: The martial renown of Vandals rested upon exhaustive drilling and veteran battlefield cohesion during the turbulent close of the 4th century. Core tactical doctrine integrated heavy shield formations with disciplined skirmishing wings, executing tactical maneuvers designed to absorb and counter enemy shock. Along vulnerable sectors, defensive engineers implemented field fortifications and obstacles, breaking the initial momentum of hostile assaults. Once enemy ranks faltered, armored shock reserves counter-charged under thunderous horn blasts, crushing exposed flanks with heavy swords and barbed spears. This balance of resilient endurance and ferocious striking power formed the military bedrock preserving Vandals against overwhelming regional adversaries.

The line closes at the sound of the bronze horn, each shield pressed against the next. Heavy horsemen smash into the front files, and the men behind thrust their spears through every gap. A spearman who flees the line is killed by his own file, because the formation has no room for deserters.

On the hill above the battle, the commanders study the formation from a lookout post. Victory depends on wagons reaching the wings with grain and on the battle line keeping its shape under pressure. Once the center breaks, the flanking cavalry can seal the field, and the nobles who paid for the levy will divide the plunder by rank.
